blocks.md: This lesson follows **Authenticating an Intervention** in *Supervisory Intervention* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Supervisory Intervention, § Authenticating an Intervention
blocks.md: On a shared wireless link, a legitimate `veto_path` intervention packet and an unauthorized drive-torque packet can arrive within the very same control cycle. The permission architecture must prevent an adversary or malformed network frame from seizing kinetic authority, yet it must never obstruct an authorized operator from arresting the machine before a collision. Systems engineers reconcile the two demands by classifying intervention operations according to the mechanical work they produce.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Causal intervention masking matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A takeover log is split into intervals by commit, blend-end, and stabilization timestamps, and only the stabilized human interval trains as demonstration.

questions.q: The section **Authenticating an Intervention** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A setpoint swap at commit demands an unbounded command derivative, so the enforcer blends between latched endpoints with a quintic smoothstep whose duration is set by the rate limit and paid from stopping reserve.
A takeover log is split into intervals by commit, blend-end, and stabilization timestamps, and only the stabilized human interval trains as demonstration.
Per channel, authority resolves every tick to exactly one state with the enforcer the sole actuator writer, and a four-phase request-acknowledge-commit-release handshake moves it.

Supervisory intervention transfers the right to propose on named actuator channels from the policy to an authenticated person, committed on a control tick and bounded by a lease, while every human command still passes the permission check.
